match.reason: No bank point teaches cyclic quadrilaterals; the closest, Proofs with angle properties, only covers general angle-chaining facts and not the opposite-angle or exterior-angle results for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

draft.title: Cyclic quadrilaterals
card: A cyclic quadrilateral is a four-sided shape with all four vertices on one circle.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to \(180^{\circ}\). So if one angle is \(100^{\circ}\), the angle opposite it is \(80^{\circ}\).
An exterior angle is formed by extending one side. It equals the interior angle opposite it, the one not next to it.

Example: in cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle A = 75^{\circ}\) and \(\angle B = 110^{\circ}\). Then \(\angle C = 180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}\) and \(\angle D = 180^{\circ} - 110^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, and an exterior angle matches the opposite interior angle.

a.q: \(PQRS\) is a cyclic quadrilateral with \(\angle P = 68^{\circ}\). What is \(\angle R\), the angle opposite \(P\)?
a.why: Opposite angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so \(\angle R = 180^{\circ} - 68^{\circ} = 112^{\circ}\). Choosing \(68^{\circ}\) wrongly treats opposite angles as equal.
a.clue: Opposite angles add to a straight angle.

b.q: \(ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. Side \(AB\) is extended past \(B\) to a point \(E\). If \(\angle ADC = 84^{\circ}\), what is \(\angle CBE\)?
b.why: The exterior angle \(CBE\) equals the opposite interior angle \(ADC\), so it is \(84^{\circ}\). Choosing \(96^{\circ}\) finds the interior angle \(ABC\) instead of the exterior one.
b.clue: Which interior angle is not next to the exterior angle?

wants.brief: A circle with cyclic quadrilateral ABCD inscribed. Side AB is extended past B to point E. Label the exterior angle CBE and mark the opposite interior angle ADC.
wants.why: It shows which interior angle is opposite the exterior angle.
